artboards.title: The row, and what a reading does to it

annotations.text:
A STOCK ROOM, NOT A STOCK MARKET
rp_corporations.stock is how much a corporation is HOLDING, and nobody buys a share. So falling is the opportunity: stores draining means they are consuming, which means they will pay for a haul.

That inverts the convention the shape borrows, so the palette had to go with it. Red is gone entirely — there is no bad news for someone with a cart full of ore — and green means one thing only: they are buying. A restocked corporation goes quiet instead.

THE FIVE TICKERS ARE REAL
EA, MUSE, HMMC, GOVT and SFPD are the acronyms already in rp_corporations. The list is sorted by movement, fastest-emptying first, so the corporation worth walking to sits at the top. Every number is SAMPLE — the stock column reads 0 for all five today.

HOW OFTEN IT POLLS — A RECOMMENDATION
Two clocks, and only one is always running:

• The LEDGER samples every 15 minutes, server-side. That is the history. Five rows a quarter-hour is 480 a day, about 43k across three months — nothing.

• The APP asks for current values when you open it, then every 60s while it stays open, and NOTHING while the phone is shut. A closed app costs zero.

Stock only moves when a player sells, so anything finer would be sampling silence.

THREE MONTHS, THEN GONE
The ranges stop at 3M because that is the whole record — a nightly purge drops samples older than 90 days, so there is no All to offer. 1D is 96 samples; 3M is about 8,600, so the longer ranges want downsampling on the server before they reach the phone.

ONE GAP WORTH CLOSING
A farmer cannot tell whether 302 is low, because nothing on the board says what full looks like. The trend and the 24h range are all the context this data can give.

A stock_capacity column on rp_corporations would fix it outright: the row could then read "a third full" rather than "302", which is the sentence the reader is actually trying to form. Worth deciding before this is built — it changes the row, not just the copy.

Also settled: the corporation page stays purely a number, no employee list.
